title: Sufinama - Bulleh Shah kaafi (kaafi-12), Ranjha Ranjha kardi
notes: Underlying composition by Bulleh Shah (d. 1757) is in the public domain worldwide. Sufinama's specific digital transcription, Roman transliteration, Hindi/Devanagari rendering, and any meanings/annotations are Rekhta Foundation's copyrighted editorial work and are NOT reproduced in Abshaar. Sufinama is used only to discover which poems exist and to cross-check the original verses; Abshaar produces its own transliteration and translations. Permission/collaboration outreach to Rekhta is in progress. Intended use is a non-commercial, open-source, academic project.

title: Bulleh Shah: A Selection, Rendered into English Verse
notes: English verse translations by Taufiq Rafat (d. 1998) are under copyright until ~2068; used as a PRIVATE academic reference only, NOT for public release or redistribution. Bulleh Shah's original Punjabi verses on the facing Nastaliq pages are public domain and may be transcribed. This copy was digitized by Google from a University of Michigan library original. IMPORTANT: keep Rafat's English out of any public/open-source publication of this project (see CORPUS_BUILD_LOG.md). Rafat's renderings are literary adaptations, not literal glosses (e.g. he maps the Urdu letters ain/ghain to English O/Q).

title: Sufinama - Bulleh Shah textual catalogs and source witnesses
notes: The authorized source layer contains 76 UUID-paired kaafi witnesses plus 48 source-category records across kalaam, doha, shabad, dohra, athvara, barahmasa, and holi. Language views share stable Sufinama content UUIDs, line IDs, and token-mapping IDs where exposed; redirects and unavailable requested scripts are recorded without synthesis. Rauf stated on 2026-07-12 that he works with Sufinama, that this is a collaborative research project, and that he was instructed to scrape the data. Written authorization details are not stored in the repository and are Needs verification. Treat Sufinama transcriptions/romanizations and overlapping categories as source-specific witnesses rather than silently merging them with Rafat or other editions.

title: Kafian: Baba Bulleh Shah
author_or_editor: Navtej Singh Atwal (PDF metadata; editorial role Needs verification)
notes: 149-page Gurmukhi PDF containing 160 consecutively numbered kafis. The underlying Bulleh Shah compositions are public domain, but rights in the 2017 selection, transcription, typography, and digital edition are not established. Full extracted text stays in ignored data/processed/private/ pending rights and textual verification. The embedded text layer drops or misorders some Gurmukhi characters and introduces intra-word spaces; rendered PDF pages are authoritative and every extracted record remains needs_review.

title: Politics, Poetry and Pluralism: Bulleh Shah in the Late Mughal Empire
notes: Historically focused master's thesis. Especially useful for its explicit warning that Bulleh Shah's biography and corpus are not definitively documented, its comparison of competing birthplace traditions, and its discussion of performative transmission and uncertain attribution. Treat its reconstructions as scholarship, not primary evidence.

title: Profile of Bulleh Shah
notes: Provides traditional biographical narratives, names, places, teacher relationships, and the site's content-category navigation. The page itself gives inconsistent birth-place wording (Uch in metadata; Pandoke in prose) and should not be treated as conclusive historical evidence.

title: Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah (RA), Kasur
author_or_editor: Auqaf & Religious Affairs Department, Government of the Punjab
notes: Official administrative/profile page for the Kasur shrine. Useful for present-day shrine location, public commemoration, and the official description of Bulleh Shah as a Punjabi Sufi poet associated with Shah Inayat Qadiri. It is not a critical historical biography.
